{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABX0eP2g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhBY2us", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 11, "title": "Add full initial MSX2 machine support and boot MSX2 cartridge software in the browser", "body": "## Problem

The emulator currently models MSX1 hardware, with a TMS9918A-compatible VDP, 16 KiB VRAM, MSX1-oriented memory/BIOS handling, and a lightweight built-in firmware/BASIC service. It can import supported Konami/ASCII MegaROM images, but successful mapper selection does **not** make an MSX2 game run: MSX2 software may require the V9938, more VRAM, MSX2 system/sub-ROM services, expanded slots, and MSX2-specific I/O.

A user attempted to run a 1987 Konami "Ganbare Goemon / Samurai" MSX2 cartridge and remained at a blue BASIC screen. That game is a motivating compatibility case, **not** a required copyrighted test asset or an assertion that the mapper is its only problem.

## Expected outcome

Implement a genuinely usable **MSX2 machine mode** alongside the existing MSX1 mode, entirely within the existing Rust emulator core plus its WebAssembly/browser frontend. The browser must be able to boot and execute original, independently authored MSX2-targeted Z80 cartridge test programs exercising MSX2 video and hardware; with locally selected, lawfully obtained MSX2 BIOS and sub-ROMs, it must also support normal MSX2 boot/slot/BIOS interactions needed by appropriate software.

The initial MSX2 configuration should model a typical **128 KiB V9938 VRAM** machine, at least 64 KiB main RAM, and a correct MSX2 slot/sub-ROM layout. Keep MSX1 mode working. Do not represent the Rust-only Weave BASIC service as original MSX2 BASIC or claim that every commercial game runs.

The deliverable is **working MSX2 emulation in the browser**, not merely an "MSX2" UI switch or larger framebuffer.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust` (`main`); follow its English Issue/PR templates and Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge process.
- Existing code: `crates/msx-core/src/vdp.rs`, `lib.rs`, `cartridge.rs`, `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `web/app.js`, `web/index.html`, and `tests/browser.spec.js`. Existing MegaROM mapper support (#8) and redesigned UI (#7) must be preserved.
- Currently the original built-in boot ROM is **not** a replacement for the full MSX2 BIOS/BASIC. Current external system-ROM import accepts only a single MSX1 32 KiB file. MSX2 normally uses main BIOS/BASIC plus a distinct 16 KiB sub-ROM. User-supplied proprietary ROMs must stay local and must not be committed, logged, uploaded, or bundled.
- Technical references: [MSX2 Technical Handbook](https://konamiman.github.io/MSX2-Technical-Handbook/md/Chapter1.html), [V9938](https://www.msx.org/wiki/Yamaha_V9938), and [MSX2 standard](https://www.msx.org/wiki/MSX2). Use specifications for independent implementation; do not copy third-party emulator code.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Machine configuration, slots and firmware

- [ ] Introduce explicit MSX1 / MSX2 machine configurations and reset/boot paths, retaining MSX1 as an available mode and avoiding duplicate emulator engines.
- [ ] Implement MSX2-compatible primary and expanded-secondary slot selection, inter-slot memory access and sub-ROM mapping, including the relevant slot control/register behavior. Cover mappings used by standard MSX2 BIOS/sub-ROM boot and cartridge execution.
- [ ] Support the MSX2 system firmware layout via **local-only user-supplied main BIOS/BASIC ROM and sub-ROM** (and required ROM components, if needed for the chosen machine profile). Validate sizes/layout, expose clear errors for missing or incompatible combinations, and support safe switching back to the built-in mode. Never distribute proprietary system ROMs or auto-fetch ROM images.
- [ ] Provide a license-cleared MSX2 test/boot path usable for automated testing and browser demonstration without proprietary ROMs, using original fixtures or compatible redistributable firmware under documented license terms. If using C-BIOS, correctly disclose that it does not provide original MSX BASIC.
- [ ] Implement additional MSX2 machine I/O actually required by the selected reference machine and test boot paths (e.g. relevant CMOS/RTC registers), with deterministic behavior and documentation for any optional/unimplemented peripherals. Preserve MSX1 PPI/PSG/keyboard/joystick behavior.
- [ ] Integrate the existing plain/ASCII/Konami cartridge mappers in MSX2 mode, including cartridge boot with appropriately mapped system ROMs; mapper selection alone must not be reported as successful game boot.

### V9938 video processor

- [ ] Extend the VDP to V9938-compatible operation while preserving accurate MSX1 TMS9918A modes; support at least 128 KiB VRAM and the correct extended addressing, registers/status bits, interrupts, and ports `98h`–`9Bh` including palette and indirect register writes.
- [ ] Implement V9938 80-column text, SCREEN 4–8 graphics modes (256/512 horizontal pixels, 192/212-line and relevant higher resolution modes), 16-of-512 RGB palette / direct 256-color mode, display page selection, and relevant scrolling, border, and sprite behavior.
- [ ] Implement the V9938 command engine and CPU/VDP transfers required by standard MSX2 drawing operations (fill/copy/line and applicable logical operations), with appropriate busy/status semantics, VRAM addressing, and interrupt/timing handling sufficient for reproducible MSX2 test programs.
- [ ] Update framebuffer dimensions, color conversion, pixelated Canvas scaling and Wasm interface where necessary so 256- and 512-pixel display modes render correctly without clipping, stretching or stale memory views. Retain the current browser audio and keyboard handling.

### Browser usability, validation and compatibility

- [ ] Add a discoverable MSX1/MSX2 choice and clear indicators of the active machine, selected BIOS/sub-ROM and cartridge, with straightforward local ROM import and reset behavior. Keep advanced settings appropriately tucked away; do not regress the focused UI from #7.
- [ ] Provide small, redistributable **MSX2-specific** test programs/ROM fixtures that boot in the browser and visibly exercise extended palette, 512-wide and 256-color/212-line modes, extended VRAM, sprites, VDP commands and expanded-slot/sub-ROM interactions. They must execute Z80 instructions through the core, not simulate an MSX2 screen in JavaScript. Include legal provenance for every distributed binary.
- [ ] Add deterministic Rust tests for VDP ports/registers/status, VRAM modes and command timing/results, slots/sub-ROM/BIOS and reset behavior, and MSX1 regression cases. Add Playwright end-to-end tests which boot the MSX2 browser mode, load an original MSX2 test cartridge, check actual Canvas pixel output/input/audio and prove no network upload of user files; preserve existing MSX1/MegaROM/browser tests.
- [ ] Verify the published static-app build layout remains compatible with GitHub Pages `/msx-rust/`, updating scripts, asset inventory, screenshots, docs and smoke tests as needed. Run the repository's documented format/lint/test/build/browser checks and report the actual results in the PR.
- [ ] Document exactly which MSX2 functions and common software dependencies are implemented, which remain unsupported, and that game-specific compatibility beyond verified fixtures is not guaranteed. Preserve legal ROM guidance and MSX1 behavior.
- [ ] Do not add unrelated MSX2+/turbo R features, disk/tape emulation, SCC audio or exhaustive per-game fixes unless demonstrably necessary for the MSX2 acceptance cases. Preserve a small coherent design and avoid copying existing emulator implementations.
- [ ] **Do not require the user to perform subjective game play-testing or supply copyrighted game files before PR approval/merge.** AI-verifiable builds, tests, and browser automation are the pre-merge gate.

## Optional validation

- After merge, the owner can load a lawfully obtained MSX2 system ROM and try "Ganbare Goemon / Samurai" and other MSX2 titles; record actual boot/display/audio results and create separate follow-up Issues for uncovered compatibility problems. This manual human testing is not a merge blocker.
- Compare behavior against a reference emulator or physical MSX2, and test in additional browsers where practical.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] Verify the merged MSX2 browser mode is published via GitHub Pages, and that the static site actually loads its Wasm and boots the legally distributable MSX2 fixture with visible video and working controls. Record the real deployment URL and observed outcome. This cannot be a pre-merge gate; unexpected live-site problems should be tracked as new Issues.
